title: Central fill label and the registry of partner pharmacies
subtopic: Central fill label and partner records
rule_summary: Under 21 CFR 1306.14(b) (Schedule II) and 21 CFR 1306.24(b) (Schedules III, IV and V), if the prescription is filled at a central fill pharmacy, the central fill pharmacy shall affix to the package a label showing the retail pharmacy name and address and a unique identifier (i.e. the central fill pharmacy's DEA registration number) indicating that the prescription was filled at the central fill pharmacy, in addition to the label information required by paragraph (a) of each section. Under 21 CFR 1304.05(a) every retail pharmacy that utilizes the services of a central fill pharmacy must keep a record of all central fill pharmacies, including name, address and DEA number, authorized to fill prescriptions on its behalf, and must verify the registration of each; under 1304.05(b) every central fill pharmacy must keep a record of all retail pharmacies, including name, address and DEA number, for which it is authorized to fill prescriptions, and must verify the registration of each. These records must be made available upon request for inspection by DEA.
exam_relevance: Tests who labels a centrally filled controlled-substance prescription and what extra label content identifies the central fill pharmacy, and the reciprocal partner lists each pharmacy keeps.

authority.name: Labeling of substances and filling of prescriptions
Records of authorized central fill pharmacies and retail pharmacies

common_confusions: The central fill pharmacy affixes the label, and the label shows the retail pharmacy's name and address, not only the central fill pharmacy's.
Both pharmacies keep a partner list and verify the other's registration.
verification_notes: Read on 2026-09-17 in the eCFR (Title 21 up to date as of 9/15/2026): 21 CFR 1304.05, 1306.14(b) and 1306.24(b).
